# Qualify a manufacturing or fulfillment supplier

[Overview](#overview) · [Before you start](#before-you-start) · [Steps](#steps-at-a-glance)

## Overview

Before relying on a supplier for a physical product or material customer-delivery function. An approved supplier qualification and controlled pilot with quality, capacity and continuity obligations assigned.

Start with the applicability facts and evidence listed in the first step. Resolve missing facts before authorizing the affected work. Completion requires the documented outcome, including tracked exceptions; starting an application or recording a task is not evidence of completion.

> This is an operational coordination guide. Confirm the applicable company facts, contracts and jurisdictions before acting. Qualified advisers own legal, tax, safety or regulatory determinations and any required professional work. The cited authorities describe their named jurisdictions or frameworks; their rules are not asserted for other countries. External actions require approval for the specific action.

> Editorial status: operational draft. Source pages checked on 2026-10-29. No case-specific legal review, professional assurance or completed execution is claimed.

## Step details

<a id="step-1"></a>

### 1. Define specifications and supplier requirements

agent-runnable


Prepare the product or service specification, volumes, traceability, quality, lead-time and location requirements. Identify critical materials and customer or regulatory constraints requiring specialist input.

- Sources: [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)

<a id="step-2"></a>

### 2. Collect supplier capability evidence

agent-runnable


Verify the counterparty and gather capacity, quality, test, insurance and relevant certification evidence. Distinguish a supplier claim from independently checked evidence and record gaps.

- Sources: [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)

<a id="step-3"></a>

### 3. Review quality, commercial and compliance risks

human · human approval required


Engineering, quality, operations and advisers assess samples, manufacturing controls, subcontracting, IP and local requirements. Decide which audit or site checks are needed and leave unverified capability visibly pending.

- Sources: [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)

<a id="step-4"></a>

### 4. Approve terms and a controlled pilot

human · human approval required


Authorized parties finalize specifications, acceptance, change control, tooling ownership, remedies and continuity arrangements. Approve only a bounded pilot until the required evidence is complete.

- Sources: [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)

<a id="step-5"></a>

### 5. Accept the supplier or assign remediation

human · human approval required


Evaluate the pilot against agreed quality and delivery criteria. Record the approved scope, unresolved corrective actions and review schedule, with an alternative plan for critical dependencies.

- Verify: An approved supplier qualification and controlled pilot with quality, capacity and continuity obligations assigned.
- Sources: [CPSC manufacturing best practices](https://www.cpsc.gov/business--manufacturing/business-education/business-guidance/BestPractices) · [SBA manage your business](https://www.sba.gov/counseling/manage-your-business/)
